text: When I started to use habitica I became a big fan of the app. It was my first gamified ToDo/habit management app and I really liked the idea to organise my day like a role play game! Nevertheless, things have changed for me: THE GAMIFICATION My in-game character achieved Level 100 and I played through all the quests Habitica offers in 5 month. Partly, I passed them by myself and other quest I finished with groups of 10+ fellows. For me actually there is no point to play all the quests again or to start again with a level 1 character. And there is more to criticise: I can say that a group of 10+ people makes the quests and the whole game too easy. Your character will become overpowered quite fast: If you have rogues in your group, you will drown in gold and stuff. Warriors can at some point kill most monsters by themselves. Mages are leveling up like crazy and the rest of their group will rarely be out of mana because of their spells. Healers will at some stage avoid any damage for the group but are also very useless in way as long as you can buy a healing potion for 25 Gold. Another critique I have, is about the achievements: They are hard to achieve, which is good in my point of view. Nevertheless they are also quite pointless, because they have NO effect on your game. My conclusion for the gamification part: If you are looking for a gamified todo/habit app Habitica is worth a try, but keep in mind that the gamification part is easily played through and can get quite boring at some stage. Habitica needs i.m.o more balance if you are playing in a group, it needs new (more difficult) quest and achievements which have a real additional value for the gamer. THE TODO/HABIT MANAGEMENT PART: The best thing here is that habitica differentiates between the categories "Habits", "daily/weekly/monthly tasks" and todos. If you are useing habtica with a big screen via browser you can see everything you need to do at a glance. This is really useful! On a smaller screen you need to swipe between the categories, which works quite well. The problem is that the lists in the categories can get quite long even on big screen if you have to manage more than one big project. You can help yourself with specific tags for your tasks and todos and their included checklists. That works but for me it is not the best solution: If you filter one project you lose sight of the other. Here are some features I also really missed: - Reminders cannot be added in the browser version of habitica - If you go on a holiday, there is just the possibilty to pause ALL of your habits, tasks and todos. You cannot pause them by a specific category - There is no easy option to postpone a project, a task or todo (x) hours/days/week etc. You have to change all dates manually - There is no option to limit the duration of specific daily/weekly/monthly tasks for a period of time. My conclusion here: If you need a professional app to manage all yout projects, tasks and habits habitica delivers some good ideas but is lacking quite important features imo. Sadly For me I can say that I will still use the app until my subscription ends. Afterwards I might change to ToDoIst or else if there is no real development in habitica
